name: APDS-9960 proximity, gesture & colour sensor
description: Broadcom (Avago) APDS-9960: an IR-LED proximity sensor (8-bit count), clear/red/green/blue ambient light channels (16-bit counts each) and a four-direction gesture engine, over I2C at the fixed address 0x39. Chip runs on 2.4-3.6 V (3.8 V absolute max) with 3.3 V logic. Sold as: SparkFun RGB and Gesture Sensor - APDS-9960 (SEN-12787), 6-pin header VL, GND, VCC, SDA, SCL, INT, no regulator; the purple GY-9960-3.3 clone modules use the same pin order.
eli5: Shines invisible light to tell how close your hand is, and measures how much red, green and blue light is falling on it.

pins.name: VL
pins.description: IR LED supply (3.0-4.5 V), only needed if the PS jumper is opened; with PS closed (as shipped) it is tied to VCC, so leave it unconnected

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Sensor supply, 2.4-3.6 V (3.3 V). NOT 5 V tolerant: no regulator on the board

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data, 3.3 V logic (10k pull-up to VCC via the I2C PU jumper)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock, 3.3 V logic (10k pull-up to VCC via the I2C PU jumper)

pins.name: INT
pins.description: Interrupt output, open-drain, active low; not needed for basic use

supplierQuery: APDS-9960 RGB gesture proximity sensor breakout I2C
buildNotes: Power VCC from 3.3 V only: the chip's absolute maximum is 3.8 V and the SparkFun board has no regulator or level shifter. Do not use 5 V on VCC, SDA or SCL.
With the PS jumper closed (as shipped) the IR LED runs from VCC, which must then be at least 3.0 V for the LED (VLEDA 3.0-4.5 V); 3.3 V is right.
Check the ID register 0x92 reads 0xAB (some clone chips report 0x9C or 0xA8). The address 0x39 is fixed: one sensor per I2C bus.
Write all the control registers first, then ENABLE (0x80) = 0x07 (PON + AEN + PEN); the chip takes 5.7 ms to start after PON.
Colour integration = 2.78 ms x (256 - ATIME); max count = min(65535, 1025 x (256 - ATIME)). Wait for STATUS AVALID, then read 8 bytes from 0x94: clear, red, green, blue, each low byte first.
Proximity: wait for STATUS PVALID, then read PDATA (0x9C), 0-255, higher = closer. The IR LED pulses up to 100 mA, so give the board a short, solid supply wire.
Gesture detection uses the FIFO at 0xFC-0xFF and is not covered by this driver or the simulator.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from apds9960 import APDS9960

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
sensor = APDS9960(i2c)
while True:
    p = sensor.proximity()
    c, r, g, b = sensor.color_raw()
    print('P=%d C=%d R=%d G=%d B=%d' % (p, c, r, g, b))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the proximity and the clear, red, green and blue counts set on the sliders
